correctness.rationale: Reassessed the complete corrected RESULT.md in repairs/1. The frozen headline's worked example K(infinity)=2.2516703... has incorrect digits: independent high-precision bisection of the stated first-order condition on (.01,.5) gives s=0.2366043836611758136... and K=2.251670218254316518...; for b=2 it gives K(1)=4.143338556577247605.... The corrected decimal examples use these values. The analytic theorem is unchanged. Exact rank-one cardinal replacement follows by checking the new nodal values; for the intact cardinals use the derivative of the nodal polynomial proportional to (z^2-1)U_{n-1}(z). In a bulk compact angular offset the cosine difference divided by the offset is the negative angular mesh times an average sine, uniformly bounded away from zero after removing the mesh factor. This proves the multiplicative compact sinc approximation even at its zeros. Evaluating at the moved node and its retained neighbor yields the distinguished pair 2|sinc(u)|/epsilon times 1+o(1), up to a uniformly bounded additive term. For the other cardinals, the exact product shows their local terms at |r| larger than a fixed bound are |sinc(u)| |u-delta| [1/|r|+O(1/r^2+1/n)] in a bulk fraction of the mesh on both sides. Nearby noncolliding indices contribute O(1), and beyond that bulk fraction each term is O(1/n), including the removable offset u=0. Consequently the two-sided harmonic contribution is precisely 2|sinc(u)| |u-delta| log n+O(1). Globally the cosine difference factorization yields |L_m|<=C/(1+|u|), so the far-field limsup of the normalized Lebesgue function approaches the intact 2/pi upper coefficient, strictly below a local witness. Compact localization and strict concavity of sin(pi s)+b sin(pi s)/s on (0,1/2), plus reflection and comparison of other offsets, then give convergence of all global maximizers and the exact logarithmic coefficient. The removed grid point matches the upper constant 2 in the collision regime, since the intact cardinal sup tends to one and the off-pair mass at y is O(epsilon log n). The repair also supplies explicit uniform bounds |L_m(y)| comparable to epsilon and |L_{m+1}(y)| bounded for 0<epsilon<1/2, and uses the local harmonic witness and removed point for the two uniform lower bounds, rather than invoking a convergent-epsilon limit for that quantifier. The frozen checker was read and not executed; its finite tolerances do not certify the printed decimals. Replay the numerical check with bisection of pi(s^2+bs)cos(pi s)-b sin(pi s), followed by 2 sin(pi s)(1+b/s)/pi, or use the analytic steps for the infinite claims. The original wrong decimal is preserved unchanged under source/.

value.rationale: The corrected theorem isolates a natural interpolation instability caused by two almost duplicate samples. Two amplification mechanisms balance on a genuine inverse-logarithmic scale; it gives exact global coefficients, not only lower witnesses, and proves where all worst-case evaluation points asymptotically lie. The sharp location and profile are useful in understanding the damage from a single defective sample. This survives the decimal repair and does not purport to control simultaneous defects, endpoint motion, or convergence rates.
